From: Samantha Lee <samantha@finco.com>

Subject: Severe latency spike this morning — need telemetry for exec update

Karthik —

We experienced a sustained latency spike and elevated 5xx rates across our checkout flow between 08:45–09:20 PT. This impacted throughput and caused a few customer-facing errors. Our CRO is asking for a short exec summary + raw evidence we can share with their security & compliance team.

Can you provide:
- A timestamped slice of request/response traces for 08:30–09:30 PT, including error codes and token counts
- The retention window for runtime request logs and where an export lives (S3 path or drive link)
- Any inferred root cause (resource saturation, model OOMs, network retries) you can confirm quickly

We need something we can wire into a 10:30 AM call. Please tell me what you can hand over now vs what needs more time.

—Samantha

[attachment: screengrab-finco-ops-08-50.png (PNG 240KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-10-05T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency spike this morning — need telemetry for exec update

Samantha — thanks for the flag and the screenshot. I'm triaging now. Quick answers up front: we can produce a timestamped trace export for the window and a perf snapshot that contains GPU metrics, RPC latency histograms, and request ids within ~40 minutes.

Immediate next steps I am taking:
- Pulling continuous-batcher traces for the FinCo model routes for 08:30–09:30 PT (will include request_id, model_variant, seq_len, tok_in/tok_out, error codes)
- Generating a performance archive (perf-snapshot-20271005.tar.gz) with host-level metrics and kernel-level OOMs if present
- Confirming retention policy: per-customer runtime traces are kept 90 days in hot storage, 365 days in cold archive; recent 7 days are indexed for fast export

Marissa/Vivek — can you confirm whether we should provide raw traces or a redacted packet for legal? Laura — looping you for the exec summary language and whether this needs legal hold.

Karthik

[attachment: request-ids-stdin.txt — list of extracted request_ids]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-10-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency spike this morning — need telemetry for exec update

Karthik — thanks. Quick operational notes:
- We have preliminary traces exported to an internal Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/finco/incident-2027-10-05/traces (access controlled)
- The perf snapshot includes sample KPS/RPC histograms and per-GPU memory utilization. No kernel OOMs flagged in the initial pass; there were short-lived enqueue latencies on a single host (host-3) that correlate with a higher retry rate to the backend cache.
- Raw traces contain API keys and some prompt snippets; per FinCo request we should produce a redacted packet for broader sharing.

Action items for the call:
1) Provide Samantha a one-pager with timeline + high-level cause (retry storm -> cache contention on host-3 -> transient queueing)
2) Provide an export of redacted traces + perf-snapshot (I will sanitize prompt text and PII)
3) Confirm retention/chain-of-custody for the artifacts if FinCo legal requests evidence for audit

Vivek — can you package the sanitized export and include a short statement describing our log retention policy and checksum of the exported archive? I'll draft the timeline doc for execs.

Marissa

Marissa/Team — packaging the sanitized export now. Notes for chain-of-custody and evidence:
- Export created: perf-snapshot-20271005.tar.gz (contains traces.ndjson, host-metrics.csv, rpc-histograms.json)
- Checksum (sha256): 3f9b2c7a... (placeholder until final archive created)

I'm attaching the packaged snapshot to this thread for immediate download (attached). Sending checksum in follow-up.

—Vivek
